title: Banpará says its security system blocked a cyberattack and Pix, suspended as a precaution, is returning
date_note: Diário do Pará's report of 25 November says the attack was identified on the night of Monday (23).
geo_basis: Bank named by the source; no city stated in the page, pin at Belém, capital of the bank's home state Pará
summary: Diário do Pará reports that Banpará's security system detected atypical Pix movements in an account linked to Sefa, blocked the suspicious operations and recovered the amounts, according to the bank. President Ruth Melo said the bank suspended all Pix preventively and that it was returning. The bank gave no amount or technical details, and other banking operations were normal.
plain: A Brazilian state bank says it stopped suspicious Pix transfers from an account linked to Sefa and paused Pix as a precaution. Pix is being restored, per the bank's president.
exec: A bank's instant-payment service was paused after suspicious transfers, which the bank says it blocked and recovered; it gave no amount or technical detail.

validation.note: Only Diário do Pará read; the bank's statements are as relayed by it, no Banpará own page read.
